title: How the ZIA Terraform provider detaches references before deleting objects
aliases: terraform delete group still associated with rule
group deleted but rule still references it

prose.text: Before deleting a group, the provider edits the rules that reference it to drop the group. {{helper-purpose}} {{helper-callers}} The helper is generic in shape, but what it sweeps is fixed by its caller. {{helper-sweeps-firewall-filtering-rules-only}} {{helper-label-selects-nothing}}
Related provider behavior that also reports success without confirming the result is in [[zia.terraform.rule-order]], and staged changes after a write are covered in [[zia.terraform.activation]].

checks.do: Which DNS control rules hold a DNS application group before destroying it (`applicationGroups`), and detach it by hand or in the same plan.
Which firewall filtering rules hold a network service group before destroying it (`nwServiceGroups`), and detach it by hand or in the same plan.
Whether the rules that used a destroyed group were re-read afterwards, rather than trusting a successful apply.
Whether ZIA refuses or accepts a delete of a group that live rules still reference.
Whether the ID-only match can strip an entry for an unrelated object type from a rule.

helper-purpose.statement: Before deleting a group-like object, the provider runs a shared helper whose stated purpose is to avoid the API's RESOURCE_IN_USE refusal by removing the object's ID from the rules that reference it.

helper-sweeps-firewall-filtering-rules-o.statement: The helper lists firewall filtering rules and nothing else, and its getter and setter closures are typed on the firewall filtering rule model. It cannot see DNS control rules or any other policy.

helper-label-selects-nothing.statement: The `resource` string a caller passes to the helper is used only in a log line. Which field is swept is decided entirely by the getter and setter closures.
helper-label-selects-nothing.conditions: Absence claim: read the whole helper body at both refs; `resource` appears in the signature and in the one log call quoted here, and nowhere else.

quotes: log.Printf("[INFO] Detaching filtering rule from %s: %d\n", resource, id)

helper-callers.statement: Nine resources call this helper on delete: DNS application groups, IP destination groups, IP source groups, network application groups, network services, network service groups, location management, rule labels, and users.
helper-callers.conditions: Count from `git grep -n DetachRuleIDNameExtensions` over zia/ at v4.8.3 and at the pin; both refs list the same nine call sites plus the declaration. Only the DNS application group and network service group sites are quoted in this subject; the other sites were not audited for field choice.

dns-group-delete-sweeps-src-ip-groups.statement: Deleting a DNS application group calls the helper with closures over the firewall filtering rule's `SrcIpGroups` field, for both reading and writing. The "DNSApplicationGroups" label does not change that.

dns-rule-model-has-application-groups.statement: In the Go SDK, the DNS control rule model has its own `ApplicationGroups` field (JSON `applicationGroups`), separate from the firewall filtering rule model that the helper sweeps. The SDK comment and the provider documentation both describe it as the DNS application groups the rule applies to.

quotes: // DNS application groups to which the rule applies
`application_groups` (List of Objects) DNS application groups to which the rule applies

dns-group-references-not-detached.statement: So deleting a DNS application group never removes the group from the DNS control rules that use it. The detach step edits only firewall filtering rules, and the delete follows regardless.
dns-group-references-not-detached.conditions: Depends on no other code in the delete path touching DNS control rules (the delete function body at both refs contains only the helper call and the group delete). What ZIA then does with a group that rules still reference is gap in-use-enforcement.

upstream.note: Filing 4 (delete-path protection gaps) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

dns-group-delete-can-strip-unrelated-sou.statement: The same sweep removes any entry whose numeric ID equals the DNS application group's ID from the source IP groups of every firewall filtering rule, a different kind of object.
dns-group-delete-can-strip-unrelated-sou.conditions: Code shows the match is on ID alone. It matters only if a DNS application group and an IP source group can share a numeric ID, which depends on how ZIA allocates IDs across object types (gap id-namespace).

upstream.note: Filing 4 (delete-path protection gaps) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

service-group-delete-sweeps-nw-applicati.statement: Deleting a network service group calls the helper labelled "NwApplicationGroups", with getter and setter closures over the firewall filtering rule's `NwApplicationGroups` field.

filtering-rule-model-separates-service-g.statement: In the Go SDK, the firewall filtering rule model has separate `NwApplicationGroups` and `NwServiceGroups` fields.

service-group-references-not-detached.statement: So deleting a network service group never removes the group from the `nwServiceGroups` of the firewall rules that use it, and the delete follows regardless.
service-group-references-not-detached.conditions: Depends on no other code in the delete path touching nwServiceGroups (the delete function body at both refs contains only the helper call and the group delete). What ZIA then does with a group that rules still reference is gap in-use-enforcement.

upstream.note: Filing 4 (delete-path protection gaps) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

service-group-delete-can-strip-unrelated.statement: The same sweep removes any entry whose numeric ID equals the network service group's ID from the network application groups of every firewall filtering rule, a different kind of object.
service-group-delete-can-strip-unrelated.conditions: Code shows the match is on ID alone. It matters only if a network service group and a network application group can share a numeric ID, which depends on how ZIA allocates IDs across object types (gap id-namespace).

upstream.note: Filing 4 (delete-path protection gaps) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

get-failure-skips-update-silently.statement: For each rule that references the object, the helper first re-reads the rule. If that read fails, the rule is skipped: the update is inside `if err == nil`, and the failure is neither logged nor returned.

quotes: for _, destGroup := range getResources(&rule) { if destGroup.ID != id { ids = append(ids, destGroup) } else { shouldUpdate = true } }
if err == nil { _, err = filteringrules.Update(ctx, service, rule.ID, &rule) if err != nil { return err } } } } return nil }

reread-result-discarded.statement: The re-read is only an existence gate: its result is discarded, and the update sends the rule copy taken from the earlier listing.

five-second-sleep-per-rule.statement: For each rule that references the object, the helper sleeps five seconds before re-reading the rule.

quotes: for _, destGroup := range getResources(&rule) { if destGroup.ID != id { ids = append(ids, destGroup) } else { shouldUpdate = true } }
if shouldUpdate { setResources(&rule, ids) time.Sleep(time.Second * 5) _, err = filteringrules.Get(ctx, service, rule.ID) if err == nil {

sleep-adds-time-per-referencing-rule.statement: The sleep comes before the re-read that may skip the rule, so it is spent even for a skipped rule, and a delete waits five seconds for every rule that references the object.
sleep-adds-time-per-referencing-rule.conditions: Read from the order of the sleep, the re-read and the update inside the helper's loop; the provider does not state the cost.

delete-follows-detach.statement: Both callers quoted here delete the object whenever the helper returns no error, and the helper returns no error for a rule it skipped because the re-read failed, so such a rule does not stop the delete.

masked-read-failure-reaches-delete.statement: So a transient failure re-reading one referencing rule leaves that rule attached, yet the group delete is still attempted. The operator sees either an opaque in-use refusal on the delete or, if ZIA allows it, a deleted group still referenced in policy.
masked-read-failure-reaches-delete.conditions: Depends on how ZIA answers a delete of an object that rules still reference (gap in-use-enforcement); the code comment in helper-purpose says it refuses, but no captured source states it for every object type or states what happens when it does not refuse.

upstream.note: Filing 4 (delete-path protection gaps) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

other-detach-callers-same-shape.statement: The other seven callers of the helper (IP source groups, IP destination groups, network application groups, network services, location management, rule labels and users) have the same shape: they return the helper's error if there is one and otherwise delete the object.
other-detach-callers-same-shape.conditions: Found by a pattern search over the provider's resource files at the pinned ref (each Delete returns on the helper's error, then calls the SDK delete); not quoted.

in-use-enforcement.title: How ZIA treats deleting an object that rules still reference
in-use-enforcement.blocks: stating whether a missed detach shows up as a failed delete or as a dangling reference
in-use-enforcement.detail: The provider's own comment quotes a RESOURCE_IN_USE refusal for a group. No captured source says this holds for DNS application groups and network service groups, or for references held by DNS control rules. Test in a scratch tenant: reference a group from a rule, delete the group directly, and re-read the rule.

id-namespace.title: Whether numeric IDs of different ZIA object types can collide
id-namespace.blocks: stating whether the ID-only match can strip a reference to an unrelated object
id-namespace.detail: The helper matches on numeric ID alone. Whether, for example, a DNS application group and an IP source group can have the same ID depends on server-side ID allocation, which no captured source describes. Compare IDs across object types in a scratch tenant.
